cockpit-frame.png.prompt:
Use case: background-extraction
Asset type: production game menu foreground, transparent PNG, landscape 16:9, 2560x1440.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: existing spaceship observation window menu background. Separate its fixed cockpit foreground from the space outside. Keep the same composition, geometry, worn ivory metal, burnt orange accents, heavy black brush inks, scratches, cables, comic crosshatching and lower floor. Remove ALL the stars, nebula, moon, outer space: replace the entire open window inside the frame with actual alpha transparency. The frame, side structures and bottom deck remain opaque. Retain thin irregular frame edges faithfully, no interior dark rectangle or haze. No new objects, no text. This image will be drawn over a moving starfield. Preserve the open central 75 percent. Do not draw checkerboard; real transparent background in the window.

space-panorama.png.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: horizontally seamless repeating space panorama texture for slow game menu panning, 3:1 landscape 3840x1280.
Input image 1 is STYLE and space/planet reference only. Create just the OUTER SPACE that lies outside this cockpit: no cockpit, no window frame, no floor, no UI. Extend it into an expansive dark quiet horizontal starfield, dirty ivory pinprick stars, sparse halftone dust/nebula with a small fractured rocky moon on the right third. The moon is wholly inside the image away from edges, diameter about 35 percent of image height. Scratchy inked British science-fiction comic illustration, heavy brush outlines and crosshatching on moon, subtle amber/sepia, near-black negative space. Most of the panorama remains near-black and low contrast for menu labels. LEFT AND RIGHT EDGES MUST TILE SEAMLESSLY with matching stars/dust density and matching black tone; no moon or distinctive structures crossing those vertical boundaries. Space only, no foreground geometry or text. This is a cyclic horizontal scrolling texture, not a screenshot.
space-panorama.png.runtime_repeat: Alternating mirrored copies ensure a continuous left/right loop.

crt-terminal.png.revision_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: production transparent game CRT terminal sprite, same 1122x1402 canvas.
Input image is the EDIT TARGET. Keep its CRT television housing, straight-on screen aperture, mechanical ceiling stalk, colours, inked comic rendering and their exact positions and dimensions unchanged. Make the cabling MUCH more abundant and visually prominent: a tangled mass of at least twelve distinct loose black and ivory insulated leads, thick ribbed cable bundles, long hanging U-shaped loops, doubled slack loops and curly coiled telephone-style cables. They drape from the ceiling mount, spill out to BOTH SIDES of the mechanical stalk through the large currently empty upper half, loop and coil down toward the television shoulders, with several loose unplugged connectors visibly hanging. Add more overlapping coils and loops below the housing too, staying inside the original canvas. Use the broad transparent space on either side of the stalk for a luxuriant asymmetric cable silhouette, not a neat single straight cable. Let the metal mechanical arm remain visible among the spaghetti. Keep ALL new cables outside the glass content aperture and outside front control knobs. Do not obstruct or alter the screen. Maintain clear actual transparency between individual cables and outside the silhouette. Heavy black brush inks, crosshatching, scratched dirty ivory and muted burnt orange, same comic art as original. No text, no portrait, no QR baked in.
crt-terminal.png.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: reusable game HUD CRT terminal sprite, transparent PNG, portrait 1024x1280.
Input images are STYLE REFERENCES only. One front-facing chunky CRT television in a battered ivory/charcoal metal housing, restrained burnt-orange details, bolted plates, heavy black brush ink contours, dry-brush scars, crosshatching and halftone shadows, matching the supplied science-fiction comic HUD. It hangs from the ceiling on an absurdly overengineered articulated mechanical stalk: telescoping struts, hydraulic pistons, large joints, brackets, and loose cables draping alongside and below the television. Orthographic FRONT VIEW, screen faces directly at viewer, rectangular flat content aperture with gently rounded outer glass surround. Entire silhouette in frame, isolated against actual transparency. Mechanical stalk connects to top edge of canvas, television lower centre, a few short loose cable loops hang below it. The screen content aperture should occupy x=16% to 78% of canvas width and y=42% to 79% of canvas height, a large clear almost-square dark charcoal green screen with no glare/scanlines so code can overlay an avatar+username or a perfectly readable QR code. Screen remains straight and level, no perspective slant. No text, letters, numbers, portrait or QR code baked in. Transparent outside the housing and arm; keep aperture dark opaque. Equal clear margins around housing. The thick casing and right-hand knobs should not intrude inside the screen content aperture.
